investigations.question: When a replica that does not itself hold the value recovers instance (replica A, instance i), does the recovery adopt the value that prepare replies report as accepted/pre-accepted, or does it replace that value with a NOOP?
investigations.hypothesis: startRecoveryForInstance sets inst.vbal to the newly tried ballot and puts its own PrepareReply (VBallot = that ballot, Status/Command from its own possibly empty local state) first into lb.prepareReplies; the adoption loop only takes replies with VBallot >= the running candidate ballot, so genuine replies at the real value ballot are skipped and the recovery proceeds to sub-case 6 with a NOOP command.
investigations.discriminator: Whether a permitted execution can reach recovery at a replica whose crtInstance[A] >= i while its own instance holds no command (no pre-accept, e.g. it only received an Accept because the pre-accept peer set and accept peer set differed); and whether the emitted PreAccept after recovery carries Command NOOP while a delivered prepare reply carried the accepted command at a lower vbal.

investigations.hypothesis: makeBallot gives every non-designated replica a fixed recovery ballot (r.Id for the instance owner, r.Id+N otherwise), so a recovery whose accepting peers have a higher stored bal is rejected on every attempt: each reply returns before the quorum append, no sub-case is dispatched, no further message is emitted, and the periodic retry repeats the identical Prepare ballot; only r.IsLeader (set by the master's BeTheLeader RPC) lets the ballot climb above maxRecvBallot, after which the same call joins the higher ballot and reaches the sub-case dispatch.
investigations.discriminator: Whether two consecutive startRecoveryForInstance calls on a non-designated replica emit the identical Prepare ballot while every matching reply carries the peers' higher stored bal and the replica emits no PreAccept, Accept or Commit for that instance, and whether invoking the target's own BeTheLeader then produces a Prepare ballot above maxRecvBallot that the peers join (producing a matching reply and a dispatched sub-case).

investigations.question: When a recovery replaces the command that a live owner had proposed and accepted locally, does the owner's client request survive through the re-propose path, and does the original instance produce any reply?
investigations.hypothesis: handleCommit re-queues the pending proposals on the owner's ProposeChan and clears them, so the client's request is not silently consumed by the replacement decision, but the original instance produces no reply because replies are emitted only when the state machine executes commands and the executed command is the NOOP.

investigations.question: Can a recovery of an instance by its own alive owner drop the instance's command when some replies at the same value ballot carry no command, and does the outcome depend on the delivery order of those replies?
investigations.hypothesis: The adoption loop takes any reply whose VBallot is at least the running candidate ballot and copies its command into the candidate, so a reply at the same value ballot that carries no command can replace the command the owner itself contributed; because the fabricated self reply is already in the appended set, the dispatch fires on the second delivered peer reply, and the candidate adopted then is handed to startPhase1 (sub-case 5/6) as the instance's command, so replies delivered after the trigger are appended to the fresh bookkeeping and cannot restore the command. On one fixed reply set with two command-carrying and two empty peer replies the owner's command therefore survives exactly when the second delivered peer reply carries it: kept for the orders 1,2,3,4 and 3,1,4,2, dropped for 1,3,4,2 and 3,4,1,2. The six permutations of the three-reply set follow the same rule: 2,4,3, 3,4,2, 2,3,4 and 4,3,2 drop the command while 3,2,4 and 4,2,3 keep it, so the completed permutation space of that reply set contains no order that contradicts the mechanism. Nothing can undo that adoption afterwards: the replies still to come are N - SlowQuorumSize, fewer than SlowQuorumSize, so the fresh bookkeeping never reaches another dispatch.
investigations.discriminator: Closed for the delivery-order axis and for the reply-set axis: all six permutations of the three-reply set and four orders of the two-carrier/two-empty set follow the reply adopted at the trigger position, the number of command-carrying replies does not decide the outcome, and a second dispatch after the trigger is arithmetically unreachable because only N - SlowQuorumSize replies can still arrive. A reply whose value ballot exceeds the fabricated candidate is the neighbouring question's territory (a recovery by a replica lacking the command ignores lower-ballot replies) and is not re-opened here.

knowledge.statement: makeBallot assigns the instance owner the ballot equal to its own replica id and any other recovering replica id+N, and advances it in steps of N only while r.IsLeader is true and the candidate is below maxRecvBallot; epaxos.New hardcodes IsLeader false and only the exported BeTheLeader RPC sets it, which the master invokes for the replica it designates. Repeating startRecoveryForInstance without that flag therefore reuses the identical ballot, whereas after the flag is set the same call emits a ballot above maxRecvBallot. For a non-owner, the boundary is the comparison between its fixed id+N ballot and the ballot the accepting peers have stored: id+N below that value is rejected inertly exactly as the owner's ballot is, while id+N above it is joined by the peers and the attempt advances.

knowledge.statement: In handlePreAcceptReply the block at epaxos/epaxos.go:876-881 overwrites lb.ballot, lb.cmds, lb.status, lb.seq and lb.deps whenever a reply's VBallot is >= the running lb.ballot, so a reply whose Status is COMMITTED replaces lb.status with COMMITTED; the guard immediately before it (epaxos/epaxos.go:870) returns for any reply while lb.status is neither PREACCEPTED nor PREACCEPTED_EQ, so every later reply to the same PreAccept is discarded and lb.preAcceptOKs stops increasing, leaving the leader's proposal in the pre-accept state for that attempt. knowledge.statement: handleCommit, for the instance owner only, tests whether the committed command is a single NONE operation and whether the local leader bookkeeping still holds pending client proposals; when both hold it pushes every pending proposal back onto the replica's own ProposeChan and clears lb.clientProposals, so the client request is re-proposed on a new instance instead of being consumed by the committed NOOP. The re-queued proposal keeps the same command id and reply writer, and the new instance's decision and execution deliver the client reply, while the replaced instance itself produces no reply because its proposals were cleared.

knowledge.statement: A nil command slice does not stay nil across the wire: PrepareReply.Unmarshal (and the other RPC decoders) allocate the received slice with make([]state.Command, alen1), so a sender that carries no command yields a non-nil empty slice at the receiver. In handlePrepareReply's adoption loop that empty slice is copied into lb.cmds, and the sub-case 5/6 fallback tests only `inst.lb.cmds != nil`, so it passes the empty slice to startPhase1 instead of substituting state.NOOP(); the resulting instance holds an empty (non-nil) command list, which executeCommands accepts because its guard is also a nil test, and handleCommit's re-offer path does not recognise it because that path requires exactly one command with operation NONE. Which command is adopted is the one carried by the last reply appended before len(lb.prepareReplies) reaches SlowQuorumSize; the recoverer's own fabricated reply is already appended, so with one self reply the trigger falls on the second delivered peer reply, and the dispatch hands the instance to startPhase1 with fresh bookkeeping, so replies delivered after the trigger are appended to that new bookkeeping and never enter the decision. Measured on one fixed reply set with two command-carrying and two empty peer replies, the owner's command survives exactly when the reply at that trigger position carries it - kept for the delivery orders 1,2,3,4 and 3,1,4,2, dropped for 1,3,4,2 and 3,4,1,2 - so neither the first delivered reply nor the number of command-carrying replies decides the outcome. Replies delivered after the trigger cannot re-open the decision, and not only because the instance status has already moved: the dispatch consumes the bookkeeping, the fresh bookkeeping startPhase1 installs begins with no appended replies (measured as lb_appended 0 right after the trigger and 1, then 2, as the two post-trigger replies of the four-reply runs land in it), and the replies that can still arrive after the trigger number N - SlowQuorumSize, which for every N is smaller than SlowQuorumSize itself, so a second dispatch on that bookkeeping is unreachable in this path rather than merely unobserved.

knowledge.statement: In the captured EPaxos package the value a recovery adopts is not protected by the quorum that holds it: four distinct mechanisms of the same recovery path each let a recovering replica end up proposing, and then deciding, a value other than the one its prepare replies carry. (a) startRecoveryForInstance fabricates a value ballot for its own state - the recoverer's own id when it is the instance owner and id + N when it is not, without advancing while IsLeader is false - and the adoption loop then honours only replies whose value ballot is at least that fabricated one, so a non-owner recoverer's fabricated ballot sits above the peers' stored value ballots and its genuine replies are skipped (measured: replies at value ballot 0 were passed over against a fabricated ballot of 8), while an owner recovering its own instance fabricates its own id, which equals the peers' value ballot, so their replies are still adopted - the case (d) depends on (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451, 1145-1165, 1239-1246). (b) A reply whose value ballot is below the running candidate ballot - which begins at the recoverer's pre-recovery local value ballot and rises to the fabricated recovery ballot as the loop adopts - is ignored even when it reports the highest accepted value, so a NOOP replaces an accepted value, including one another live replica has already committed; a reply whose value ballot equals the running candidate is still adopted, which is what lets an empty reply replace the command in (d). (c) A reply that reports the instance COMMITTED is discarded once its status reaches lb.status, because the pre-accept guard then rejects the remaining replies, so the first recovery attempt stalls until the retry (epaxos/epaxos.go:870-881, 1255-1313). (d) A reply that carries no command decodes as a non-nil empty slice, which the sub-case 5/6 fallback passes to startPhase1 instead of state.NOOP() (epaxos/defs.go:228-235, epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1311), and the adopted value is the one carried by the last reply appended before the appended count reaches SlowQuorumSize - the fabricated self reply counts toward that threshold, so the trigger falls on the second delivered peer reply and the dispatch then replaces the bookkeeping, so replies delivered afterwards cannot restore the command; the owner's command therefore survives exactly when that second peer reply carries it, measured on one fixed reply set with two command-carrying and two empty peer replies as kept for the orders 1,2,3,4 and 3,1,4,2 and dropped for 1,3,4,2 and 3,4,1,2. Recovering replicas that already hold the value are not affected by (a)-(b), and the client re-offer protects the single-NOOP case but not the empty-slice case.
knowledge.conditions: N=5, F=2 configuration of the captured snapshot with Thrifty on and IsLeader false at the recovering replica; the instance owner fails inside its accept window and the recovering replica holds the instance without its command, or (for the arrival-order variant) recovers its own instance while replies at the same value ballot differ.

scope.description: Five replicas (F=2) constructed in-process with the package's own field and RPC-table initialization, without peer sockets and without the run() loop, so handler execution is deterministic. All inter-replica traffic is the package's own marshaled RPC structs: each bcast runs SendMsg into a captured byte buffer and every delivery decodes a fresh object from those bytes, preserving the transport serialization boundary; delivery is FIFO per link and messages to a crashed replica are dropped. The executed scenario is: replica 1 pre-accepts a conflicting command on its own instance (2,0); leader replica 0 proposes X (PUT key 1) on instance (0,0); replica 1 replies non-equal then crashes; replica 0 runs the Accept phase at ballot 0 to replicas 2 and 3; replica 0 crashes after the Accept broadcast and before consuming any AcceptReply; replica 3 (which received only the Accept, holds no command, and has crtInstance[0] == 0) calls startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) as its own executor would after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD; the quiescent message exchange is then completed.
assumptions: Replica construction mirrors epaxos.New minus peer connections, the run() loop and ComputeClosestPeers, so PreferredPeerOrder is the constructor order (id+1+i) mod N.
InstanceSpace rows hold 32 entries instead of MAX_INSTANCE (10M); only instances 0..2 are used, so no code path indexes beyond the allocated row.

The auxiliary broadcast of replica 1's conflicting proposal is discarded; only its local conflict state (conflicts[2][key 1]) is used as the premise that makes the leader's pre-accept reply non-equal and therefore forces the Accept phase.

Crashes are modelled as: the replica stops consuming messages, no further message is delivered to it, and every other replica's Alive flag for it is cleared, matching the target's mechanism for deciding broadcast recipients.
Replica 3's recovery is invoked through startRecoveryForInstance, the same function the target's executor invokes from instancesToRecover after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD.
excluded: No client connection path, no execution of the state machine, no recovery timer loop, and no master/BeTheLeader designation (IsLeader stays false, as epaxos.New sets it).

basis.prefix: The harness builds five in-process replicas, injects the conflicting premise at replica 1, runs replica 0's proposal of X through the package's own startPhase1/bcastPreAccept/handlePreAcceptReply/bcastAccept path, delivers the Accept to replicas 2 and 3, crashes replicas 1 and 0, then calls replica 3's startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) and delivers the resulting Prepare/PrepareReply traffic through the package's own handlePrepare/handlePrepareReply. Every outgoing message is decoded from the bytes SendMsg flushed, so message content, ballot fields and commands are the target's own values.
basis.requirement: A recovery of instance (0,0) must not replace with a different value the value that the collected prepare replies report as accepted or pre-accepted; the recovering coordinator adopts the value carried at the highest value ballot among the replies (including its own state) and re-proposes that value if it must restart phase 1.
basis.responsibility: The recovering coordinator's own adoption rule (epaxos/epaxos.go:1236-1313) and startRecoveryForInstance's construction of its self reply (epaxos/epaxos.go:1142-1168), not the client or the environment: the leader's crash after broadcasting Accept is a permitted failure, and the value X was accepted at ballot 0 by replicas 0, 2 and 3 in the executed scenario.

comparisons.description: The command the recovery proposes for instance (0,0) equals the PUT carried by the prepare reply with the highest value ballot (the quorum-held value X); violated when the recovered PreAccept carries the NOOP (cmd_op 0) although quorum_reply_command_op is 1.

A replica that held X after the Accept phase still holds X once the recovered proposal has run to quiescence; violated when the live holder ends up with the NOOP (cmd_op 0) because the recovered PreAccept overwrote its command.

scope.description: Five replicas (F=2) built and driven as in the value-adoption harness (in-process replicas with the package's own handlers and marshaled RPC structs, FIFO delivery, no delivery to crashed replicas). scope.description: Same 5-replica harness as the recovery-ballot experiment. Owner replica 0 proposes X on instance (0,0) and enters the Accept phase at ballot 0 towards replicas 2 and 3 (replica 1's non-equal reply is delivered first and replica 1 then fails); replica 0's AcceptReplies are left in flight; replica 2 then recovers the instance at its own ballot 7, so the accepting peers store bal 7, and replica 2 fails after broadcasting that Prepare. Two further recovery attempts are then made at replica 1 and replica 3, whose fixed ballots for a non-owned instance are 6 and 8 respectively, and each attempt's Prepare/PrepareReply traffic and follow-up messages are recorded.
assumptions: Same construction, transport boundary and crash model as the value-adoption and recovery-ballot experiments; in-process replicas, marshaled RPC structs decoded per delivery, FIFO per link, no delivery to crashed replicas.
The two recoverers hold the instance (replica 1 pre-accepted X and answered the owner's Prepare; replica 3 received the owner's Accept), which is what lets their executors act on it.
No production logic is modified; IsLeader stays false for both recoverers.
excluded: No client path, no state-machine execution, no run() loop or recovery timer loop in the harness.

basis.prefix: The harness drives the owner's proposal and accept phase through the target's own path, delivers replica 2's higher-ballot Prepare so the peers store bal 7 and then fails replica 2, and finally calls startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) first at replica 1 and then at replica 3, delivering each attempt's Prepare/PrepareReply traffic through handlePrepare/handlePrepareReply and recording tried, matching and follow-up messages.
basis.requirement: Recovery must be attainable by any replica that holds the instance: a recovering replica whose fixed ballot is below the ballot the accepting peers have stored must still be able to advance the instance, either by a prepared quorum and a sub-case dispatch or by a later attempt using a ballot above the stored one.
basis.responsibility: The target's own ballot policy (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451 makeBallot) and its rejection handling (epaxos/epaxos.go:1204-1235 handlePrepareReply): the peers answer honestly with the ballot they stored and the recoverers are ordinary replicas.

comparisons.description: A non-owner recoverer whose fixed ballot (6) is below the peers' stored ballot (7) still advances the instance: no matching reply and no follow-up message means the attempt is inert; violated in this configuration.

Control: a non-owner recoverer whose fixed ballot (8) is above the peers' stored ballot (7) produces matching replies and dispatches its phase-1 proposal; expected to hold, locating the boundary at the comparison between the recoverer's fixed ballot and the stored ballot.

scope.description: Owner replica 0 proposes X on its own instance (0,0), replica 1's non-equal pre-accept reply is delivered and replica 1 then fails, so the owner enters the Accept phase at ballot 0 towards replicas 2 and 3; replica 3 accepts without ever pre-accepting (its state holds no command), and the owner's AcceptReplies are left in flight. The owner, alive and still holding X, then runs startRecoveryForInstance(0,0); the harness delivers the Prepare replies of replicas 2, 3 and 4 in a chosen order (replica 2 carries X at value ballot 0, replicas 3 and 4 carry no command at the same ballot) and records whether the owner re-proposes a command and what its instance holds afterwards. The test runs the same message set twice with the empty reply last in one run and first in the other.
assumptions: Same construction, transport boundary and crash model as the other experiments in this harness.
Delivery order among the prepare replies is chosen by the harness, which is what a real network does not fix; the read order is not altered.
No production logic is modified.
excluded: No client path, no state-machine execution, no run() loop or recovery timer loop.

basis.prefix: The harness drives the owner's proposal and accept phase through the target's own handlers, fails replica 1 after its reply, delivers the Accept to replicas 2 and 3, then calls the owner's startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) and delivers each collected PrepareReply to the owner, recording the owner's leader-bookkeeping state (status, appended count, nacks, prepared flag) and the instance's command length before and after the dispatch.
basis.requirement: A recovery of an instance must not drop the instance's command when a reply without a command arrives at the same value ballot as replies that carry one, and the adopted value must not depend on the delivery order of equally admissible replies.

comparisons.description: After the owner's recovery of its own instance, the instance still holds a command (its own X); violated when the instance is left with no command even though the owner's own reply carried it.

scope.description: Owner replica 0 proposes X on its own instance (0,0) and replica 1's non-equal pre-accept reply is delivered, so the owner enters the Accept phase at ballot 0 towards replicas 1 and 2; both accept, replica 1 with status PREACCEPTED and replica 2 with status PREACCEPTED_EQ, while replicas 3 and 4 hold the instance with no command. interpretations.rationale: Current account: the recovery path in the captured EPaxos package can replace a quorum-held value with a NOOP, contrary to its own stated case analysis. Basis is source-level: (1) epaxos/epaxos.go:1145 sets lb.ballot to the pre-recovery local vbal, then :1150-1153 call makeBallot and overwrite inst.vbal with lb.lastTriedBallot, and :1154-1165 append a self PrepareReply carrying that new ballot as VBallot together with inst.Status/inst.Cmds (NONE/nil for a replica that never pre-accepted, e.g. one whose only knowledge of the instance is an Accept, epaxos/epaxos.go:995-1005, which stores Deps/Seq/bal/vbal but neither Cmds nor a status). (2) epaxos/epaxos.go:1239-1246 adopts values only when reply.VBallot >= the running candidate and processes the self-reply first, so a genuine remote reply whose VBallot is the real value ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1191-1201 reports inst.vbal unchanged by the prepare) is skipped once the fabricated self-ballot is larger. (3) With lb.status still NONE, :1278-1279 selects sub-case 6 and :1307-1313 calls startPhase1 with state.NOOP() because lb.cmds is nil, i.e. the recovery proposes a different value for the instance even though the reply set carried the accepted/pre-accepted one. The code's own comment at :1228-1235 states that these sub-cases (including '2 -> accepted' and '3 -> pre-accepted ... and allEqual') are meant to take replies' values into account, so the fabricated self-ballot defeats the documented case analysis for any coordinator that lacks the value itself. Scope of the claim: the recovery proposes NOOP instead of the quorum-held value; whether the NOOP then reaches a majority and erases the accepted value at every live replica (and thus produces two different decisions for instance (A, i) versus the crashed leader's state) is the next discriminator, not asserted here. Limits: not executed; the reachability premise (a coordinator knowing the instance without holding the command) is registered as a necessary gap; the ballot comparison also means a genuine reply with a value ballot above the coordinator's own recovery ballot is still adopted, and recovery by the replica that itself pre-accepted the value does adopt it (its self-reply carries the real Status/Cmds), so the defect is bounded to coordinators that lack the value.
counterevidence: epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451: makeBallot climbs above maxRecvBallot when IsLeader is true, so the master-designated leader (epaxos/epaxos.go:1121-1125) gets a ballot above existing ones; that does not remove the fabrication (the self-reply is still the top ballot in its own reply set), but a designated leader's recovery is what keeps the ballot from being permanently rejected, so it must not be confused with the adoption defect.

epaxos/epaxos.go:1255-1303: when the recovering replica itself holds the pre-accepted value (thrifty keeps the accept peer set a subset of the pre-accept peer set, epaxos/epaxos.go:510-513 and 571-586), the self-reply carries that value and sub-cases 1-3 can still complete the instance; the value loss is therefore not universal to all recoveries.
limitations: No execution receipt: the account rests on source reading of the captured snapshot (fixed revision), not on a completed witness.

The scenario in which the recovering replica knows the instance without its command is sourced but not yet demonstrated; it requires the accept-phase peer set to differ from the pre-accept peer set (peer liveness change between the two broadcasts) or an equivalent observer.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: in the executed scenario the captured EPaxos package loses an accepted value during recovery of the instance by a replica that does not itself hold the command, and decides a different value for that instance. Witnesses from receipt 143e14592eea4c42b3c81044e3860348 (fixed experiment fc825b4d2a9c488e8c03dff32b05cab7-experiment, test TestAssuranceEPaxosRecoveryValueAdoption, 24 parsed events, no parsing errors): event 5 shows leader 0 in status ACCEPTED with cmd_op 1 after the non-equal pre-accept phase; event 6 shows the Accept broadcast to replicas 2 and 3 at ballot 0; event 7 shows replica 2 carrying the PUT (cmd_op 1) at vbal 0 after the Accept, event 8 shows replica 3 holding the same coordinates with no command (has_cmds false, status NONE) and vbal 0, and event 9 shows leader 0 still ACCEPTED with cmd_op 1 immediately before it fails. The instance (0,0) value was therefore accepted at ballot 0 by replicas 0, 2 and 3, i.e. by a quorum of the five replicas, and no replica had committed it when leader 0 failed after the Accept broadcast. Event 11 records the recovery start by replica 3: tried_ballot 8 and its own self reply carrying self_vballot 8 with self_status NONE and self_has_command false, while startRecoveryForInstance had set lb.ballot to the pre-recovery local vbal (epaxos/epaxos.go:1145) and had overwritten inst.vbal with the freshly tried ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1150-1153, anchor s-decl-recovery). Events 12 and 13 show the Prepare broadcast at ballot 8; event 14 shows replica 2's PrepareReply carrying the PUT at vballot 0 (status PREACCEPTED_EQ) with Ballot 8 after joining, and event 15 the reply of replica 4 with no command; event 16 states the decisive operands: self_vballot 8, max_remote_vballot_with_command 0, so the self ballot is above every remote value ballot, and quorum_reply_command_op 1. Comparison 0 is violated with complete witness 17: the PreAccept the recovery emitted (ballot 8, cmd_len 1) carries cmd_op 0, i.e. state.NOOP(), while quorum_reply_command_op is 1 - the adoption loop at epaxos/epaxos.go:1239-1246 (anchor s-decl-prepare-reply) keeps lb.cmds nil and lb.status NONE because the self reply is evaluated first with the fabricated vbal 8 and the genuine reply at vbal 0 fails the >= test, so sub-case 6 (epaxos/epaxos.go:1278-1279) calls startPhase1 with the NOOP (epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1313). Events 18-21 show the consequence: the recovered NOOP became the instance's value at replicas 2, 3 and 4 (status 4 COMMITTED, cmd_op 0), the quiescent run completed, and comparison 1 is violated with complete witness 20: replica 2, which held the accepted PUT after the Accept phase (event 7), ended holding the NOOP (cmd_op 0), i.e. the recovery overwrote the only live copy of the accepted command. Events 22 and 23 record the failed replicas' retained state: replica 1 still PREACCEPTED with cmd_op 1 and leader 0 still ACCEPTED with cmd_op 1, so the recovered decision (NOOP at ballot 8) is a different value for instance (0,0) than the value those replicas accepted at ballot 0. This establishes the scoped defect: after a permitted leader failure in the accept window, a recovery driven by a replica that knows the instance without its command proposes and commits a NOOP instead of the value the prepare replies carry, discarding a quorum-accepted value rather than completing it.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: in the captured EPaxos package the ability to recover an instance whose stored ballot is above the recovering replica's own ballot depends on the master-designated IsLeader flag; without it the replica's retry repeats an identical rejected prepare and the recovery dispatches nothing at all. Witnesses from receipt 911d45335b3047178a6fd739f24b2cfb (fixed experiment adfa9c6d31ca481896e5ca1277f6cdf4-experiment, test TestAssuranceEPaxosRecoveryBallotProgress, 36 parsed events, no parsing errors): events 0-2 establish the premise that the owner's pre-accept replies were not equal (acceptor 1 answered with status PREACCEPTED while acceptor 2 answered PREACCEPTED_EQ), leaving owner replica 0 with status ACCEPTED and cmd_op 1; event 3 shows the owner's Accept broadcast at ballot 0 to replicas 1 and 2, and events 4-5 show those replicas recording the accepted coordinates at bal 0 with cmd_op 1. Events 6-10 show replica 2 recovering the same instance at its own ballot 7; events 11-14 show replicas 0, 1, 3 and 4 joining that ballot (bal 7) without any accepted value at 7, and replica 2 was failed before consuming the replies, so the instance stayed uncommitted while the quorum's stored ballot was 7. Event 16 records the owner's first recovery round with is_leader false and max_recv_ballot 7; events 17-19 are the three peer replies, each carrying Ballot 7 while the owner tried ballot 0, so all three were rejections; event 20 is the decisive result: tried_ballot 0, prepare_ballots [0,0,0], stored_bal_before_attempt 7, prepare_ballot_above_stored_bal false, appended_replies 1 against slow_quorum 3, subcase_dispatched false, follow_up [] and instance_status 3 - the recovery emitted nothing and the instance stayed accepted but uncommitted. Events 21-25 repeat the same attempt through the executor's retry path with identical operands (tried_ballot 0, the same three Ballot-7 replies, appended_replies 1, no follow-up), which satisfies the repeated-nonprogress condition rather than a single artificial timeout. Event 26 is the target's own authority transition (BeTheLeader handler, is_leader true); event 27 starts round 3 with max_recv_ballot 7, events 28-30 show the peers joining the climbed ballot 10 and answering with matching Ballot 10, event 31 shows appended_replies 3 >= slow_quorum 3, subcase_dispatched true and follow_up [accept, accept], and event 32 shows the owner COMMITTED with cmd_op 1 (X preserved), with events 33-35 recording the same committed value at replicas 1, 3 and 4. Declared comparisons: 0 and 1 are violated with complete witnesses 20 and 25 (the retarded attempts neither dispatch a sub-case nor use a ballot above the stored one), and the control comparisons 2 and 3 hold (evaluated indices 31 and 32). The scoped defect is therefore the authority gate itself: the ballot that can act on an instance whose stored ballot is higher is only acquirable with the master-designated IsLeader flag, so an ordinary replica - here the instance owner, whose fixed ballot is its own id - cannot recover such an instance and emits no follow-up of any kind.
counterevidence: The blocker is a peer-side stored ballot left by a failed recovery coordinator; it is not a general inability to recover. An updated client retry or another replica that knows the instance can still act: replicas with a fixed ballot above the stored one (id+N > 7, i.e. replicas 3 and 4 with ballots 8 and 9) would not be rejected by this mechanism, and the designated-leader control in this very receipt shows the recovery completing with the accepted value X.

The peers' answers in rounds 1 and 2 are legitimate protocol behaviour, not a fault: each reports the ballot it stored (7) and the recovering replica's 0 was genuinely below it, so the rejection does not by itself demonstrate a violation of the peer's duty.
The defect requires the higher-ballot record to pre-exist; in this run it came from a recovery attempt that failed after broadcasting its Prepare, which is a permitted failure but a specific one.

Because handlePrepare does not advance crtInstance, replicas 3 and 4 knew of instance (0,0) only as a placeholder after the ballot-7 Prepare and would not have been triggered by their own executors in this run, so no other replica attempted the instance here; the claim therefore rests on the retry behaviour of the replica that ran the recovery, not on a measured statement about every replica in the system.
limitations: One configuration and one extreme case: N=5, F=2, instance (0,0), and the recoverer is the instance owner, whose fixed ballot is 0, the lowest possible; the same mechanism was not exercised for a non-owner recoverer (id+N) or for a stored ballot between the two.

The harness delivered the owner's Prepare and the peers' rejections explicitly and re-invoked startRecoveryForInstance instead of waiting for the executor's COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD retry (epaxos/epaxos.go:404-417 was not run), so the retry cadence is modelled, not measured.

The premise state (peers storing bal 7 with an uncommitted instance) was produced by failing replica 2 after its Prepare broadcast and discarding its replies; the harness schedules that delivery rather than relying on real transport timing.

The authority in the control comparison came from invoking the target's own BeTheLeader handler directly; the master's designation policy, its reassignment after a replica is detected dead, and the case of a live but non-designated replica were not exercised.
No client is present: the claim concerns the recovery attempt's messages and the instance's state, not a measured client-visible latency or completion interval.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: the executed run supports the status-guard mechanism and shows the stall, and the same source path predicts that a later attempt completes a NOOP commit that contradicts the live committed value. Evidence from receipt 9b8471479d484a12bdaf961653bbbe54 (test TestAssuranceEPaxosRecoveryContradictsCommittedValue): index 11 shows replica 2 holding instance (0,0) COMMITTED with cmd_op 1; index 16 shows its prepare reply to the recovering replica 3 carrying vballot 0 with Status COMMITTED and a command; index 19 shows the recovery nevertheless emitting a PreAccept with cmd_op 0 (the NOOP), and index 21 shows replica 3 ending in status PREACCEPTED, i.e. undecided after the run - comparison 1 of that experiment is violated with witness 21. The mechanism is sourced: the adoption block epaxos/epaxos.go:876-881 replaces lb.status with the reply's COMMITTED status on the restarted phase-1 path, and the guard at epaxos/epaxos.go:870 then returns for every later reply that carries a matching ballot, so lb.preAcceptOKs stops at one and neither the fast nor the slow commit branch is entered; the second acceptor in this run did handle the PreAccept and reply (index 23 shows replica 4 holding the NOOP as PREACCEPTED_EQ), so the missing quorum is not a missing reply. limitations: Source-only account: no execution exercised the branch, and the harnesses of this run never produced a status >= ACCEPTED instance without a command.

Receipt 81a44ff62122417db3cc5697fc5303f6 (fixed experiment 0757162a4aa64ef4a58a90002641eb27-experiment) shows the owner holding its command X at status ACCEPTED before its own recovery (index 0), the empty acceptor at status NONE after the Accept (index 3), and, after the owner recovered its own instance and the three PrepareReplies were delivered, an instance left at status PREACCEPTED with an empty command list plus bookkeeping whose candidate command is an empty slice (index 4: inst_cmds_len 0, inst_status 1, lb_cmds_len 0, lb_status 1, lb_appended 1, lb_nacks 0), with no command proposed afterwards (index 5) and the same values in the second run (indices 9-11); comparison 0 and comparison 1 are both violated with witnesses 5 and 11. The mechanism is now sourced: a reply from a replica that holds no command carries a nil command slice, the decoder allocates it with make([]state.Command, alen1) so the receiver sees a non-nil empty slice (epaxos/defs.go:228-235), the adoption loop copies that empty slice into lb.cmds because its VBallot equals the running candidate ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1239-1246), and the sub-case 5/6 fallback substitutes state.NOOP() only when lb.cmds is nil (epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1311), which an empty slice is not - so startPhase1 is called with an empty command batch and the instance becomes PREACCEPTED with Cmds of length zero (epaxos/epaxos.go:1291-1296, 751-779). Consequences for the captured package: the instance is proposed and can be decided with no command at all, replacing the command the owner itself held; executeCommands accepts an empty non-nil batch because its guard is a nil test, so the instance executes as a no-op rather than stalling; and the client re-offer path that protects the fabricated-NOOP case does not fire here, because handleCommit tests for exactly one command with operation NONE (epaxos/epaxos.go:1090-1099), which an empty batch never satisfies. The mechanism is now sourced: a reply from a replica that holds no command carries a nil command slice, the decoder allocates it with make([]state.Command, alen1) so the receiver sees a non-nil empty slice (epaxos/defs.go:228-235), the adoption loop copies that empty slice into lb.cmds because its VBallot equals the running candidate ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1239-1246), and the sub-case 5/6 fallback substitutes state.NOOP() only when lb.cmds is nil (epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1311), which an empty slice is not - so startPhase1 is called with an empty command batch and the instance becomes PREACCEPTED with Cmds of length zero (epaxos/epaxos.go:1291-1296, 751-779). After the recovery dispatch, the replies that can still arrive are the peer replies not yet delivered, N - SlowQuorumSize of them, because the recoverer's own reply plus the first SlowQuorumSize - 1 peer replies were consumed by the dispatch; for N=5 that is two replies against a threshold of three, and since N - (N+1)/2 is smaller than (N+1)/2 for every N, no configuration of this path can re-reach the threshold on the fresh bookkeeping. interpretations.rationale: Current account: the status-guard mechanism is executed on the first recovery attempt - the recovering replica adopts the COMMITTED status of a peer's pre-accept reply, discards the remaining replies and stays undecided - and the executor's retry then proceeds because the local value-ballot token has moved, so the stall is per-attempt rather than permanent; the retry's completion is the value-adoption defect's contradiction. Evidence: receipt 9b8471479d484a12bdaf961653bbbe54 (first attempt) shows replica 2 holding (0,0) COMMITTED with cmd_op 1 (index 11), its prepare reply reporting that status with a command (index 16), the recovery nevertheless proposing the NOOP (index 19), and the recovering replica ending PREACCEPTED (index 21; comparison 1 of that experiment violated with witness 21) while the second acceptor had handled the PreAccept and replied (index 23). Receipt d80cbfd9f9a547639811aeacb19c0a30 measures the retry: the second attempt's prepare replies match its ballot (index 22 from replica 2 with Status COMMITTED, index 23 from replica 4), three replies are appended and the dispatch happens (index 24: instance status ACCEPTED), and the retry commits the NOOP (index 25: replica 3 COMMITTED with cmd_op 0; index 27: replica 4 the same) while replica 2 keeps X committed (index 26). The mechanism is sourced: the adoption block epaxos/epaxos.go:876-881 overwrites lb.status with a reply's COMMITTED status on the restarted phase-1 path, and the guard at epaxos/epaxos.go:870 then returns for every remaining reply carrying a matching ballot, so lb.preAcceptOKs stops at one and neither the fast nor the slow commit branch is entered on that attempt; on the next attempt the coordinator's own vbal token equals the tried ballot, so the COMMITTED reply is no longer adopted, the reply is counted, and sub-case 3 (epaxos/epaxos.go:1269-1272) leads to the accept phase that commits the NOOP. The binding was re-checked: the retry receipt comes from an experiment owned by the recovery-value question, so by the association rule this account keeps its conditional conclusion and cites that receipt under the recorded joint-history reasoning instead of binding the experiment here.
counterevidence: The stall is per-attempt, not permanent: the measured retry dispatches and commits, so the mechanism delays the recovered proposal by one executor interval rather than blocking it forever.

The peer holding X is protected in its own state (epaxos/epaxos.go:1082), so the status-guard mechanism itself does not rewrite that replica; the contradiction arises from the recovery's own fabricated value.
The peer's COMMITTED status is the target's own honest answer; the defect lies in the recovering side's handling of that answer, not in the peer's reply.
limitations: One configuration and one instance (0,0) with N=5, F=2 and one command; the guard's interaction was not exercised for a leader that holds its own command, nor with a lower ballot on the COMMITTED reply.

The recovering replica's own instance reaches a decided state only after the retry, and dependents of (0,0) at that replica were not executed.

The mechanism is now sourced: a reply from a replica that holds no command carries a nil command slice, the decoder allocates it with make([]state.Command, alen1) so the receiver sees a non-nil empty slice (epaxos/defs.go:228-235), the adoption loop copies that empty slice into lb.cmds because its VBallot equals the running candidate ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1239-1246), and the sub-case 5/6 fallback substitutes state.NOOP() only when lb.cmds is nil (epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1311), which an empty slice is not - so startPhase1 is called with an empty command batch and the instance becomes PREACCEPTED with Cmds of length zero (epaxos/epaxos.go:1291-1296, 751-779). That also explains why the probe recorded no PreAccept command (proposed_cmd_op -1 was the empty batch, not an absent proposal) and why the probe's two runs coincided: the empty slice wins in both delivery orders because the loop adopts ties with >= and the empty reply is adopted whatever its position, the last delivery being irrelevant. Consequences for the captured package: the instance is proposed and can be decided with no command at all, replacing the command the owner itself held; executeCommands accepts an empty non-nil batch because its guard is a nil test, so the instance executes as a no-op rather than stalling; and the client re-offer path that protects the fabricated-NOOP case does not fire here, because handleCommit tests for exactly one command with operation NONE (epaxos/epaxos.go:1090-1099), which an empty batch never satisfies. A second receipt measures the client-side consequence of exactly that decision: receipt 098ab4425325464192aa558be557f0ce (fixed experiment 49b316fdc67c459fb374500fb7f26514-experiment) attaches a real client proposal (command id 91) to the owner's own instance, that instance's own recovery decides the empty batch, and both declared comparisons are violated with complete witness 4 - the decided instance holds a command list of length zero while the owner held command X before (index 0: status 3, cmd_op 1) and the owner's pending request is never re-offered (requeued 0 with pending_proposals 1 and reply_bytes 0), while the single-NOOP decision of the same family (receipt 893f6180a4514a8d9e20a1d5e6698542) re-queued its request and later completed it. The contrast is the re-offer guard's own condition: handleCommit requires exactly one command with operation NONE (epaxos/epaxos.go:1090-1099), which an empty batch never satisfies, so the empty-command decision drops the client's request with neither a reply nor a re-offer. The delivery-order question is now measured with three runs of the same reply set (receipt e89ecb076e8d4a78b174f848562ed77f, fixed experiment e8fb81e1cb0742118ce33f60e08a0de1-experiment): with the replies delivered as 2,4,3 the instance ends with no command (comparison 0 violated, witness 6); as 3,4,2 the same outcome (comparison 1 violated, witness 13); and as 3,2,4 - where the command-carrying reply is the second delivered - the instance keeps the owner's command (comparison 2 holds, evaluated 20). The mechanism is therefore not a simple last-reply-wins rule over the whole set but the timing of the quorum trigger: handlePrepareReply dispatches as soon as len(lb.prepareReplies) reaches SlowQuorumSize, which for one self reply and a five-replica configuration is two peer replies, and the candidate command is whatever the last adopted reply in that prefix carries. In this reply set two peers carry no command and one carries X, so two of the three delivery orders put an empty reply in the adopted position and lose the command, while the third order puts X there and keeps it. The adopted value therefore depends on arrival order among equally admissible replies rather than on their content, and the empty-slice handling is what makes the losing orders lose the command outright instead of substituting state.NOOP(). The earlier statement that the order variant was unmeasured is withdrawn; the state/command invariant entry is qualified rather than wrong: it holds for the command-carrying writers, while this path reaches the same status-without-command combination through an empty non-nil slice, which that entry's nil test does not cover. The deciding position is now observed rather than derived, with a four-order receipt on a fixed reply set that holds two command-carrying and two empty peer replies (receipt 251562364ca64b3c80cd14e0d6aeddc3, fixed experiment e25f403842234594881914f730efff4e-experiment, test TestAssuranceEPaxosRecoveryMixedQuorumOrder, exit 0, 40 parsed events, no diagnostics). The harness reads the recoverer's leader-bookkeeping pointer before and after every delivery, so the trigger is observed as the delivery that replaces that object: in all four orders the replacement happens on the second delivered peer reply - index 5 for the order 1,2,3,4 with reply 2 carrying the command, index 15 for 1,3,4,2 with reply 3 carrying none, index 25 for 3,4,1,2 with reply 4 carrying none, index 35 for 3,1,4,2 with reply 1 carrying the command - and the fresh bookkeeping that startPhase1 installs already carries the decision (fresh_lb_ballot -1, fresh_lb_status 1, fresh_lb_cmds_len 1 when the trigger reply carried the command and 0 when it did not). The outcomes then follow that position and nothing else: comparison 0 holds for 1,2,3,4 (index 9: owner_cmds_len 1, proposed_cmd_op 1, trigger reply 2); comparison 1 is violated for 1,3,4,2 with complete witness 19 (owner_cmds_len 0, proposed_cmds_len 0), where the first delivered reply carried X while the trigger reply did not, so a command-carrying reply present when the trigger fires does not protect the command and the empty reply need not arrive first; comparison 2 is violated for 3,4,1,2 with complete witness 29, where both command-carrying replies are delivered after the trigger and the instance stays empty although there are now as many command-carrying as empty peer replies in the set; and comparison 3 holds for 3,1,4,2 (index 39: owner_cmds_len 1, trigger reply 1) although the first delivered reply carried nothing and the empty replies outnumber the command-carrying one in the queue before the trigger. The reply set is fixed across the four runs, so the number of command-carrying replies does not decide the outcome: the trigger prefix holds the recoverer's own reply plus two peer replies, and the owner's command survives exactly when the second peer reply carries it. The three-order tie receipt that left half the permutation space open is now completed (receipt 2ba5ed477d854a01adbca361e9a8a918, fixed experiment 1479f8725fce4b139838cfa202f7a2a1-experiment, test TestAssuranceEPaxosRecoverySameBallotOrder, exit 0, 42 parsed events, no diagnostics): with the same reply set as the earlier tie runs, the orders 2,3,4 and 4,3,2 put an empty reply at the trigger position and lose the command (comparison 0 violated with complete witness 27; comparison 2 violated with complete witness 41), while 4,2,3 puts the command-carrying reply there after an empty first delivery and keeps it (comparison 1 holds, evaluated 34). Together with the three orders of the earlier receipt, all six permutations of this reply set follow the trigger position - 2,4,3, 3,4,2, 2,3,4 and 4,3,2 drop the command, 3,2,4 and 4,2,3 keep it - so the completed permutation space contains no order that contradicts the mechanism. The last axis the question still listed as unmeasured is closed by counting rather than by a new run. After the recovery dispatch, the replies that can still arrive are the peer replies not yet delivered, N - SlowQuorumSize of them, because the recoverer's own reply plus the first SlowQuorumSize - 1 peer replies were consumed by the dispatch; for N=5 that is two replies against a threshold of three, and since N - (N+1)/2 is smaller than (N+1)/2 for every N, no configuration of this path can re-reach the threshold on the fresh bookkeeping. The four-order receipt already measured the first half of that: after the trigger its fresh bookkeeping held no appended replies (lb_appended 0) and then one and two as the two remaining replies landed in it, with no further dispatch and the instance unchanged. So the empty-command adoption is final once the trigger fires, and the remaining discriminator item is answered as structurally impossible rather than unmeasured. The execution side of that decision is pinned to source as well. An instance that is COMMITTED with a non-nil zero-length command list passes every guard on the executor's path: executeCommands leaves it alone rather than routing it to recovery because its status is at least COMMITTED and its Cmds are non-nil (epaxos/epaxos.go:398-404), executeCommand admits it once its status is COMMITTED (epaxos/exec.go:24-30), and strongconnect refuses only a nil slice (epaxos/exec.go:76-78). The loop that applies a batch is bounded by len(w.Cmds) (epaxos/exec.go:122-127), so a zero-length batch applies nothing, writes no reply even where the instance still holds pending proposals, and the instance is nevertheless marked EXECUTED at the end of its SCC block (epaxos/exec.go:132); executeCommands then advances ExecedUpTo over it (epaxos/epaxos.go:398-402 and 421-423), so the instance neither stalls its row nor comes back through recovery, and the instances queued behind it become executable. The client-visible effect therefore has two independent causes: the reply write sits inside the per-command loop, which never runs for a zero-length batch, and the re-offer guard is not satisfied because handleCommit requires exactly one command with operation NONE. The executor anchors used in this account are now registered materials rather than bare line numbers: the executor's admission guard, the nil-slice check in the SCC walk, the batch-application loop and the driver loop that advances ExecedUpTo. The executor ranges registered for this account were checked against the snapshot; the admission guard is now also registered as the exact function bounds (epaxos/exec.go:25-42), while the nil-slice check, the batch-application block and the driver loop were confirmed as they stand. The two neighbouring entries that touch the same path were re-read against this account and need no change: the ballot-gated adoption entry names NOOP substitution only for a nil candidate, which is the branch its own condition describes, and the rejection entry states the nacks-before-append rule and the two IsLeader-gated restarts that the receipts support. The decoding claim was tightened by inspection: the same run-time slice allocation appears in a second decoder of the same file (PreAccept.Unmarshal, epaxos/defs.go:362-366), which is now a registered source.

The loss is still a specific interleaving: it requires an empty reply to be the second delivered peer reply, and the four orders were chosen by the harness rather than sampled from a network, so the runs show that the outcome is fixed by that position and not how often such an interleaving occurs.

The reply set is fixed across the four runs, so the number of command-carrying replies does not decide the outcome: the trigger prefix holds the recoverer's own reply plus two peer replies, and the owner's command survives exactly when the second peer reply carries it. The three-order tie receipt that left half the permutation space open is now completed (receipt 2ba5ed477d854a01adbca361e9a8a918, fixed experiment 1479f8725fce4b139838cfa202f7a2a1-experiment, test TestAssuranceEPaxosRecoverySameBallotOrder, exit 0, 42 parsed events, no diagnostics): with the same reply set as the earlier tie runs, the orders 2,3,4 and 4,3,2 put an empty reply at the trigger position and lose the command (comparison 0 violated with complete witness 27; comparison 2 violated with complete witness 41), while 4,2,3 puts the command-carrying reply there after an empty first delivery and keeps it (comparison 1 holds, evaluated 34). Together with the three orders of the earlier receipt, all six permutations of this reply set follow the trigger position - 2,4,3, 3,4,2, 2,3,4 and 4,3,2 drop the command, 3,2,4 and 4,2,3 keep it - so the completed permutation space contains no order that contradicts the mechanism. The last axis the question still listed as unmeasured is closed by counting rather than by a new run. After the recovery dispatch, the replies that can still arrive are the peer replies not yet delivered, N - SlowQuorumSize of them, because the recoverer's own reply plus the first SlowQuorumSize - 1 peer replies were consumed by the dispatch; for N=5 that is two replies against a threshold of three, and since N - (N+1)/2 is smaller than (N+1)/2 for every N, no configuration of this path can re-reach the threshold on the fresh bookkeeping. The four-order receipt already measured the first half of that: after the trigger its fresh bookkeeping held no appended replies (lb_appended 0) and then one and two as the two remaining replies landed in it, with no further dispatch and the instance unchanged. So the empty-command adoption is final once the trigger fires, and the remaining discriminator item is answered as structurally impossible rather than unmeasured. The execution side of that decision is pinned to source as well. An instance that is COMMITTED with a non-nil zero-length command list passes every guard on the executor's path: executeCommands leaves it alone rather than routing it to recovery because its status is at least COMMITTED and its Cmds are non-nil (epaxos/epaxos.go:398-404), executeCommand admits it once its status is COMMITTED (epaxos/exec.go:24-30), and strongconnect refuses only a nil slice (epaxos/exec.go:76-78). The loop that applies a batch is bounded by len(w.Cmds) (epaxos/exec.go:122-127), so a zero-length batch applies nothing, writes no reply even where the instance still holds pending proposals, and the instance is nevertheless marked EXECUTED at the end of its SCC block (epaxos/exec.go:132); executeCommands then advances ExecedUpTo over it (epaxos/epaxos.go:398-402 and 421-423), so the instance neither stalls its row nor comes back through recovery, and the instances queued behind it become executable. The client-visible effect therefore has two independent causes: the reply write sits inside the per-command loop, which never runs for a zero-length batch, and the re-offer guard is not satisfied because handleCommit requires exactly one command with operation NONE. The executor anchors used in this account are now registered materials rather than bare line numbers: the executor's admission guard, the nil-slice check in the SCC walk, the batch-application loop and the driver loop that advances ExecedUpTo. The executor ranges registered for this account were checked against the snapshot; the admission guard is now also registered as the exact function bounds (epaxos/exec.go:25-42), while the nil-slice check, the batch-application block and the driver loop were confirmed as they stand. The two neighbouring entries that touch the same path were re-read against this account and need no change: the ballot-gated adoption entry names NOOP substitution only for a nil candidate, which is the branch its own condition describes, and the rejection entry states the nacks-before-append rule and the two IsLeader-gated restarts that the receipts support. The decoding claim was tightened by inspection: the same run-time slice allocation appears in a second decoder of the same file (PreAccept.Unmarshal, epaxos/defs.go:362-366), which is now a registered source. Closing checks on this account: the harness draft is identical to the frozen basis of the last fixed experiment and to its scratch copy, so a future revision starts from the reviewed text; the status-guard account next door rightly carries no experiment binding because its retry receipt belongs to another investigation's experiment.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: a recovery driven by a replica that does not itself hold the instance's command replaces the value carried by its prepare replies with a NOOP, and the replacement can be executed to a completed contradiction of a value another live replica has committed. Three executed witnesses bound the trigger. (1) Receipt 143e14592eea4c42b3c81044e3860348 (fixed experiment fc825b4d2a9c488e8c03dff32b05cab7-experiment): the accepted value X at ballot 0 is replaced; the self reply's fabricated VBallot 8 shadows the genuine reply at value ballot 0; sub-case 6 selects startPhase1 with state.NOOP(); the holder loses X (comparison 1 violated, witness 20). (2) Receipt d80cbfd9f9a547639811aeacb19c0a30 (successor experiment d9390caf51ee413aaf05a733db9b99ff-experiment): the owner commits X (index 6) and its Commit reaches only replica 2 (index 10), so a live replica holds X COMMITTED (index 11); the recoverer's prepare reply reports X with Status COMMITTED at value ballot 0 (index 16); the recovery still emits the NOOP (index 19); the first attempt stalls (index 21); the executor's retry dispatches (index 24) and commits the NOOP at replicas 3 and 4 (indices 25, 27) while replica 2 keeps X (index 26) - two live replicas hold different decided values for instance (0,0) (comparison 0 violated, witness 25). (3) Receipt 893f6180a4514a8d9e20a1d5e6698542 (fixed experiment 6fbba03eb3354cf384e0044c37ac7542-experiment) shows the same replacement with the instance owner alive throughout: replica 0 keeps its command X in its own instance (index 2) and its own prepare reply carries it (index 3), yet replica 3, which holds no command for the instance, proposes the NOOP (indices 6, 7) and the recovered decision is installed on the live owner as a COMMITTED NOOP (indices 9 and 12), with the pending client request re-offered on a new instance (index 10) and later completed (index 17). So the defect does not require the instance owner to fail: a live but stalled owner whose instance is recovered by a replica lacking the command loses the command, and the client's request survives only because the re-propose path re-offers it. Mechanism: startRecoveryForInstance sets lb.ballot to the pre-recovery local vbal and then overwrites inst.vbal with the freshly tried ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1145, 1150-1153), so the self reply's VBallot outranks the genuine reply at value ballot 0 and the adoption loop (epaxos/epaxos.go:1239-1246) leaves lb.cmds nil and lb.status NONE; the accepted attributes are dropped with it. Event 16 of receipt 143e14592eea4c42b3c81044e3860348 shows the adoption is a ballot ordering, not a general discard: a reply whose value ballot exceeded the coordinator's own recovery ballot would still be adopted.

The committed peer keeps its value in its own state, and the protection is the absence of a writer rather than a guard: handleCommit returns immediately when inst.Status >= COMMITTED (epaxos/epaxos.go:1082), and handlePreAccept changes nothing for such an instance because its only mutation for Status >= ACCEPTED sits behind the guard inst.Cmds == nil (epaxos/epaxos.go:807-813), which is false for a replica that holds the committed command. The contradiction is therefore between two replicas' decided values rather than a silent rewrite at the holder.

The live owner's request is not silently dropped: handleCommit re-offers its pending proposal on a new instance (receipt 893f6180a4514a8d9e20a1d5e6698542 indices 10 and 17), so the client's completion is delayed rather than lost - but the originally accepted command and its ordering are gone.

The countervailing ballot-climb path in makeBallot (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451) is gated on IsLeader, which is false in all these executions and in epaxos.New; the master-designated leader's behaviour is treated in the separate recovery-authority question.
limitations: One configuration and one instance in all three receipts: N=5, F=2, instance (0,0), one PUT command (key 1) and the NOOP the recovery generates.

The completed contradiction required the executor's retry to be invoked a second time by the harness; the contradiction itself was measured, but the executor's own retry cadence was modelled rather than run.

Reaching the recovering replica in the executed scenarios required a peer of the instance to fail so that the accept broadcast skipped it (the target's own Alive mechanism); a deployment where the accepting peers and the pre-accepting peers coincide for every replica was not shown to reach the same state.
